THE OPERATING DOMAIN

Keep the limits
beside the prediction.

Physical force accuracy is unqualified. Published-data force validation has unresolved failures. No new physical solder specimen was measured for this demonstration.

What the model calculates

One connected isolated equilibrium joint between parallel, fully wetted, pinned circular rims. Source copper supplies the lower rim as an explicit hypothesis. The opposing pad, liquid solder volume, material, offset and vertical condition are supplied separately.

A prescribed gap represents an externally held fixture. Supported normal load instead solves the isolated joint's gap under a stated downward per-joint load. Upward load support is expected there. Neither mode solves package tilt or load sharing between neighboring joints.

Why the walkthrough changes the gap

Actual ULX3S U1/J16 copper supplies the 400 µm lower pad. The upper pad and process inputs are assumptions. Both recorded hypotheses use a 400 µm upper diameter, 40 and 56 nL liquid volumes, +240 µm offset, surface tension 0.48 N/m, density 9 g/cm³ and gravity enabled.

Held gap40 nL X/Z, µN56 nL X/Z, µNNumerical fixture outcome
300 µm−184.526 / −181.284−164.385 / +13.386Only 40 nL meets the rule.
330 µm−169.063 / −227.390−170.455 / −82.276Both meet the rule.

The declared fixture rule requires lateral restoration without an upward separating force at a held gap. Negative X opposes the positive offset. Positive Z points away from the board. The gap change removes the original upward-force reason to exclude 56 nL. A freely supported package needs a different weight-support objective.

These two sampled hypotheses do not bound manufacturing uncertainty or physical error. Neither selects a production solder amount. The recorded selector displays retained results. The local workbench can compute edited inputs, clear stale results and export the exact accepted comparison.

What remains outside the model

Thermal reflow history, wetting chemistry, flux and oxides, viscosity, contact-line motion, alignment time, capture range, substrate obstacles, neighboring joints, bridging, cooled stress, fatigue, electrical reliability and manufacturing yield.

Detected pad-plane excursions block a preference, but the vertex check does not prove continuous-surface clearance. Mesh exports have their own reported volume discrepancy and do not receive a universal self-intersection proof.

What to measure next

Identify the actual hot wettable rims, upper-pad geometry, liquid solder volume, held gap and offset, alloy, temperature, density and surface tension. Then qualify the force uncertainty and measure hot force versus displacement. The local Board handoff opens /lab#board-question with these requirements.

The existing 200 µm force fixture needs adaptation and qualification for this 400 µm board joint. The separate 220 versus 270 µm twenty-joint height coupon asks whether pad sizing preserves component clearance against a 185 µm target. Wetting hypotheses and opposite arm variations can erase or reverse its nominal ranking. Neither coupon size has a qualified clearance pass. That experiment does not validate the board example's forces.

Inspect the 300 µm review and the 330 µm review for exact inputs and numerical status. The complete recorded walkthrough evidence retains both unchanged native archives, their original board material and explicit notices. Local source documentation preserves the failed physical campaign and its scope. Hashes and replay do not replace a physical test.
